label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/snapbug.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_longjump.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, C, B, C where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Upright, 23 by 23 by 34, so the overall envelope fits a drum. But the outline is a box, not a cylinder: the top and below views are a square (front, left, back, right and top views), where a 55-gallon drum is round, and the three-quarter views show flat sides and sharp vertical edges. The round form the brief asks for is clearly off.

M2.reason: Measured size is 23 x 23 x 34 units, against the brief's 34 high and 23 across: zero offset, well within 15%.

M3.reason: The brief's parts are a round body, two rolled chime hoops (top and bottom), a lid rim and a bung. The asset has six flat faces and none of the hoops, lid rim or bung, so the round-part and small-part items fail. Its one hazard stripe is painted, not modelled, and is also absent (see M4).

M4.reason: Every face is one uniform flat grey (FRONT, LEFT, TOP). Nothing reads as rust-brown or worn steel, and there is no hazard stripe at all. The brief's stripe region is missing, so the colour and material items are not met.

M5.reason: No hazard stripe, no rust, no chime lines or lid seam. The only surface is a faint mottled grey grain. None of the brief's markings or wear are there.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the rubric requires: M6 is measured apart by the line-up test (picks A, C, B, C; none picked the asset). For the record, the asset at B visibly reads as a grey box beside the three Valve props, which is a real fault the test does not measure.

M7.reason: Upright: 34 high on a 23 x 23 footprint, standing on its base in the side views. A box has no front to get wrong, so nothing in the facing is off.

M8.reason: Measured: SMAK checks pass with no errors, 12 triangles (far under twice the Valve median for a prop of this size). Every visible face is closed, with no inside-out or floating geometry in any of the ten views.
